text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.7% today, rebounding from a sharp 2.5% drop on November 23rd. The bounce appears tied to escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iran reported three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz while under U.S. escort, and Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure. These events typically tighten global oil supplies and support crude prices, which may have encouraged buyers back into energy stocks after the previous day's sell-off.

The rebound is modest and comes against a weaker two-week backdrop, partly because the broader refinery trade—which has been a major money-maker—is unwinding as refining margins compress. While geopolitical risk offers a temporary lift, the structural headwinds in refining profitability and uncertainty from the failed climate talks (which rejected explicit restrictions on fossil fuels but still reflected climate-focused sentiment) continue to weigh on the sector.
